verdicts.justification: Both repros crash identically: 'F001a EXC: TypeError cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object' (reduce=PCA(n_components=5)) and 'F001b EXC: TypeError cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object' (reduce=None), raised from matplotlib_backend.py _draw via dispatch_static returning None. plot.py:564 documents 'reduce : str, dict, class, instance, or fitted Reducer', so a 5-component instance is a documented input; the error names neither the >3-D data nor a fix.

Standalone 'hyp.reduce(new_data, reduce=model)' returned shape (30, 3) OK, but 'hyp.plot(rng.normal(0,1,(30,10)), reduce=model)' raised 'ValueError: X has 3 features, but PCA is expecting 10 features as input.' from plot.py:1756 'xform = reducer(xform, ndims=3, reduce=reduce, internal=True' -- plot re-applies the fitted model to its own already-reduced 3-column output. plot.py:564 explicitly documents 'or fitted Reducer'.

hyp.plot(DL, align=False) raised 'ValueError: unknown model: False' from plot.py:1674 via analyze. plot.py:586-592 and tools/analyze.py:59-65 both promise 'If False or None, no alignment is applied'. One nuance vs the auditor's title: the standalone align() docstrings do NOT advertise False (tools/align.py:48 says 'str or dict'; align/align.py model= says 'str, class, instance, dict, or None'), though hyp.align(model=False) and legacy align(align=False) also raise 'unknown model: False'. Core defect (documented plot()/analyze() behavior crashes) stands.
hyp.plot(x, cluster=False) raised 'ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!' from plot.py:1905, while plot.py:594 documents 'cluster : str, dict, False, or None'.

hyp.plot(x, fmt='.', n_dims=2) ran the full pipeline then crashed with 'AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_dims'' -- a matplotlib artist error with no hint that 'ndims' was meant. (Plotly variant not re-run; the matplotlib half alone substantiates the finding.)

hyp.plot(DL, normalize='none') raised 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' -- the message lists 'none' as accepted yet the value that triggered it WAS 'none'; it also names the internal 'scale_type' rather than the user-facing 'normalize' kwarg, and is an AssertionError rather than ValueError.

Integer hue=np.repeat([0,1,2],30): 'int hue: n_lines = 0 n_coll = 7', legend None, 'UserWarning: legend is not supported for continuous or matrix-valued hue; ignoring legend.' Same data with str labels: 'str hue: n_lines = 3 legend labels: ['a','b','c']'. plot.py hue docstring (lines 370-387) distinguishes 'categorical labels' vs 'continuous numeric values' but never states the dtype rule that numeric labels are always routed to the continuous path. Evidence PNG t6_hue_str.png shows the 3-group categorical rendering with legend.

hyp.plot([ (50,10), (50,7) ]) raised the raw numpy error 'ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 10 and the array at index 1 has size 7' from the reduce stage, while 'align alone OK, shapes: [(50, 10), (50, 10)]' -- hyp.align pads the same input.

One plot() call with reduce={'model':'PCA','params':{}} produced 'DeprecationWarning count: 2' (identical messages); one plot() call on unequal-row datasets with align='hyper' produced 'UserWarning count: 2' of the identical 'alignment keeps only the 40 row(s) common to all datasets...' trim warning.

plot.py:581-584 docstring: 'If ndims > 3, will plot in 3 dimensions but return the higher dimensional data.' Actual run with ndims=10 on (50,20) data: 'return type: <class 'matplotlib.figure.Figure'>' -- no data returned; higher-D data only via return_model=True.

CLAUDE.md lines 89-96 list '3. Alignment ... 4. Dimensionality Reduction'. The code is the opposite: tools/analyze.py docstring says 'manip -> normalize -> reduce -> align -> cluster (the canonical 1.0 pipeline order, GH #153)' and its legacy path (line 179) is literally 'aligner(reducer(normalizer(data...)))'. Verified via code inspection instead of re-running the auditor's numeric-equivalence script -- the stage nesting is unambiguous.
